LESSON: MAP READING AND INTERPRETATION

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Natural and Historic Built Environments
Topic 4.1: Map Reading and Interpretation
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Map Reading and Interpretation, part of Natural and Historic Built Environments in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 8 SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How can we measure distance on a map? 2. How can critical thinking be used in map interpretation?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Map Reading and Interpretation together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Social Cohesion: learners work harmoniously in groups to practice scale conversions on a topographical map.

● Critical thinking: learners use critical thinking skills necessary for map interpretation

Link to other subjects:

● Creative Arts: drawing: learners apply drawing skills in drawing diagrams of the relief and drainage features on a topographical maps

● Mathematics: learners apply calculation skills in working out the area of different places on a topographical map.
